items.project_definition: The set of structural limitations, such as composite uniqueness on user and match identifiers, ensuring data integrity.
The required security mechanism for storing sensitive authentication credentials to meet complexity and safety standards.
The temporal data type used for scheduling events and recording audit timestamps.
An example of a short-form identifier for a sports club, limited to five characters.
The logic ensuring that opposing teams are distinct, dates are future-dated for upcoming events, and scores are non-negative.
The associative links between entities, such as the connection between a game and its participating clubs or league.
The requirement that a club's name must be globally unique across the system.
The standardized time zone used for all temporal records to ensure global synchronization.
The 128-bit universally unique identifier used as the primary key for all major entities.
The set of rules enforcing unique email addresses and minimum character lengths for security credentials.
The associative entity linking a person to a specific game they wish to monitor.
The restriction preventing a single person from monitoring the same game multiple times.
